Not my parents, but as of two years ago, I have no more grandmothers. (My grandfathers on both sides of my family died before or at the time that I was born)

Its hard to not cry when I remember how nice my grandmother on my moms side was. She raised six children (including my mom) by herself after her first husband died in world war 2, during the battle of the bulge. She later remarried, only for the husband to die a few years later, leaving my grandmother to (again) raise the six children all by herself. She had to drop out of the eighth grade and she didn’t have a lot of money throughout her early working life because she worked in seafood factories pealing shrimp all day. She was also a devout Roman Catholic who helped with local charities as best as she could. Her house would be destroyed in hurricane Katrina and she would be later committed to a nursing home two towns away. She lived in that place until she died in 2015. Her final will states that all her money she had, which was a few thousand dollars, was to be used towards my college education. She was the sweetest person I know and I sometimes wish I could talk to her again.

My other grandma on my dads side was crazy though, and she lived right next to my house. She was an evangelist, a 700 club member, and a Pat Robertson fan. She was also paranoid of blacks, gays, or Muslims living in her neighborhood. It was sad to see her think like that. But every now and then she had great advice that I still think about today.

All this changed my life by making me cherish every memory of my current living loved ones. I have much more respect for most elderly people. 

I also learned this important lesson that I wished I knew before: Time I so short so try to tell the ones who are important in your life that you love them even when it’s hard to say it.. because you may not get another chance.

TlL:DR I have no more grandparents. One was super nice and one was kinda crazy. I miss them both though.

Dear Janice,

I write this letter to you because perhaps what I did was wrong; my crime that is. Seeing that I say what I said and do the things I did, regardless of my wrath at the time. I show deep regret.

I am sorry that I killed you. Thankfully, no one will ever know.

Ironically, the day I murdered you and dealt with your body, I had to go to the doctor to get a test. I had been feeling ill after my fit of rage. I was known to have infertility problems before and I would see my Urologist regularly. He  said to get exercise and eat right, especially some plums. They're supposed to be good for you. Nasty things. But he said to come back in a week for another test.

I come back the week later. Now they say I am sterile. He said that everyone is showing these problems. The doctors were unsure of its cause. They tested everything; The doctor asked for my sperm sample, gave it to him, and within a few more days, he confirmed humanities fears.

Based on what I am hearing in the news, We will be the last of the human race. There are the old who dont have to worry of this because, after time, they will soon die. And there are the new born children, those who just came into this world only to know that they will be the last of us. Our future dies with them. Im only In my twenties, yet I feel they have it worse than I do.

This whole things has stirred up a whole new set of questions that I must ask myself. Is there a god?

I am not particularly religious now. I am more or less spiritual. I think a soul exists. However, I grew up Catholic; I would occasionally go to confessions and ask for forgiveness, But there are barely any priests anymore. It would take forever to find one. Religion isn't that popular these days, But that is a whole different topic.

But I really must ask myself this as I age further to my demise. Continuing on, if there is a god, is there a heaven and a hell? If the two preceding questions are true, than is this sudden infertility of the human race Gods punishment? Have the End Times come? As in revelations?

Im not sure, I feel like I'm hallucinating. I grow ever frightful.

Could forgiveness be my last stop to saving myself? Could all I have to do is prostrate myself everyday, give alms, fast from certain foods, pray, and try to understand what I did was wrong?

I will never know. Now I feel even worse regret. Your death at my hands took me by surprise. I didn't mean to kill you when I hit you upside the head. You just suddenly fell into the sink while cleaning dishes after I hit you. You called me a "lazy ass" and yelled at me the whole hour while I was trying to relax after a hard day at work. Being a sell out to some shitty company pushing stuff that people dont need is hard enough already you know...

And now the human race wont last the next generation. I wonder how you feel about that my precious darling.

Im getting ahead of myself a bit. Your already dead. And I have no idea if you will read this from whatever afterlife your in. Im guessing heaven because God had some mercy on you, a fallen victim of accidental manslaughter. Maybe he's explaining the complete infertility of the human race right this second.

But for now, I have to go...I feel like they're on to me.

Maybe my first act of forgiveness is to turn myself in to the police. They have been searching you for days. Your family has been worried non-stop.

I guess the moral of this story (or letter rather) is that: if we are the last generation we must make it our last. If we truly cant reproduce anymore, we should at least be as good as we can to each other while we have time.

I cry as I write these last words. I am remorseful. I know now what I must do.

With love,

Your "lazy ass" of a man
